record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Concerning Expansive Systems
record.context_brief: Persistence of semi-trajectories in expansive systems
record.original_question: Let f be an expansive homeomorphism of a compact metric space M. Say that the semi-trajectory of a point x is persistent in the future if for every epsilon > 0 there exists a C^0-neighborhood N_x of f such that, for every g in N_x, there is y in M with dist(f^n(x), g^n(y)) <= epsilon for all n >= 0; define persistence in the past analogously for n <= 0. Is every semi-trajectory of every expansive system persistent in the future and in the past?

evidence.quote: However each semi-trajectory is persistent : given x ∈ M, and ε > 0 there is, Nx, a C0-neighbourhood of f such that for any g ∈ Nx, there is y ∈ M, with the property dist(f^n(x), g^n(y)) ≤ ε, n ≥ 0. This is the f persistence of x in the future. We define similarly persistence in the past. ... An open question is: are all the semi-trajectories of an expansive system persistent?
Open Problem 10.2: For an Expansive Homeomorphism is every semi-trajectory peristent in the future (in the past)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,d)$ be a compact metric space and let $f\colon M\to M$ be a homeomorphism. We say $f$ is expansive if there exists a constant $c>0$ (an expansivity constant) such that for any $x,y\in M$ with $x\neq y$ there is some $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $d(f^n(x),f^n(y))>c$. Endow the space $H(M)$ of homeomorphisms of $M$ with the $C^0$ (uniform) topology, where a basic neighborhood of $f$ consists of all $g$ with $\sup_{x\in M}d(f(x),g(x))<\delta$ and $\sup_{x\in M}d(f^{-1}(x),g^{-1}(x))<\delta$.

For $x\in M$, the forward semi-trajectory of $x$ is the sequence $\{f^n(x)\}_{n\geq 0}$, and the backward semi-trajectory is $\{f^n(x)\}_{n\leq 0}$. Say that the forward semi-trajectory of $x$ is persistent in the future if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a $C^0$-neighborhood $\mathcal{N}_x$ of $f$ in $H(M)$ such that for every $g\in\mathcal{N}_x$ there exists $y\in M$ with
$$d(f^n(x),g^n(y))\leq\varepsilon\quad\text{for all }n\geq 0.$$
Persistence in the past for the backward semi-trajectory of $x$ is defined analogously, requiring the inequality to hold for all $n\leq 0$.

Question: Is it true that for every expansive homeomorphism $f$ of every compact metric space $M$, every point $x\in M$ has its forward semi-trajectory persistent in the future and its backward semi-trajectory persistent in the past?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of the question of whether every semi-trajectory of every expansive homeomorphism is persistent in the future and in the past. While the broader area of expansive and measure-expansive systems is active, no source found explicitly settles this particular semi-trajectory persistence problem, so its current status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Measure-expansive systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of expansive and measure-expansive systems, including properties of semi-orbits, but does not resolve the semi-trajectory persistence question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on (measure-)expansive systems addresses semi-orbit behaviour but does not announce a solution to the semi-trajectory persistence question.

status_evidence.title: Expansive homeomorphism - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of expansive homeomorphisms; no mention of a resolution of semi-trajectory persistence.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on expansive homeomorphisms does not record a resolution of the persistence-of-semi-trajectories problem.
